mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points over the previous month signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp does not correlate with positive equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous two months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator for broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% over the previous month signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 0.5% does not correlate with positive equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds the inflation rate (CPIAUCSL), it signals a tightening monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > CPIAUCSL does not correlate with negative equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in PAYEMS and decrease in UNRATE does not correlate with positive equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the previous month signals weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decrease > 1% does not correlate with negative equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the previous two quarters signals robust economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during an expansionary regime.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during expansionary regimes.
